from.place: size reduction of the square-zero lifting diagram

title: Small model of a square-zero quotient diagram
statement: Let R and S be commutative rings in universes u and v, S an R-algebra, D a commutative R-algebra in any universe z, J an ideal with J² = 0, and g : S →ₐ[R] D/J [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. There exist a commutative R-algebra D₀ in universe max u v, e : D₀ →ₐ[R] D, an ideal K with K² = 0, an injective R-algebra map q : D₀/K →ₐ[R] D/J, and g₀ : S →ₐ[R] D₀/K such that q composed with the quotient map D₀ → D₀/K equals the quotient map D → D/J composed with e, and q ∘ g₀ = g.

source.place: Tag 07EB (Definition 15.38.1) supplies the motivating square-zero diagram; the small-model construction is the elementary polynomial-presentation size reduction in lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-universe-lift, not an assertion stated in Stacks.

proof.text: Choose representatives b(s) of g(s) under the surjective quotient map and form the R-subalgebra A generated by them. Algebra.small_adjoin shows that A is small in universe max u v. Take D₀ = Shrink A, with its canonical algebra equivalence t, and e the composite with the subalgebra inclusion. The map e is injective.

Let K be the inverse image of J under e. Ideal.le_comap_pow, J² = 0 and injectivity of e show K² = 0. The map from D₀ to D/J induces q : D₀/K → D/J by quotient lifting; its kernel is zero by the definition of K, so q is injective. Its composite with the quotient map is the quotient map of D composed with e.

Each g(s) is q of the quotient class of t⁻¹(b(s)), so g has image in the range of q. Restrict g to that range and compose with the inverse of the algebra equivalence onto the range furnished by injectivity of q. This gives g₀ with q ∘ g₀ = g.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_squareZero_small_model
    (R : Type u) (S : Type v) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    (D : Type z) [CommRing D] [Algebra R D] (J : Ideal D) (hJ : J ^ 2 = ⊥)
    (g : S →ₐ[R] D ⧸ J) :
    ∃ (D₀ : Type (max u v)) (_ : CommRing D₀) (_ : Algebra R D₀)
      (e : D₀ →ₐ[R] D) (K : Ideal D₀) (q : D₀ ⧸ K →ₐ[R] D ⧸ J)
      (g₀ : S →ₐ[R] D₀ ⧸ K),
      K ^ 2 = ⊥ ∧ Function.Injective q ∧
        q.comp (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R K) = (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R J).comp e ∧
        q.comp g₀ = g
